summary: TLS handshakes usually carry fairly static data such as the server certificate chain and the list of trusted certificate authorities, which can be large. This proposed standard defines a TLS extension that lets a client say it already has a cached copy, so the server can skip sending it. That makes handshakes smaller, which matters most on constrained networks and devices.

eli5.summary: When you visit a friend you already know, you do not need to show your ID every time. This lets a computer say it already remembers the long paperwork, so the other side does not repeat it.

questions: how to shrink the tls handshake
